gen-dafont-impact-label-instrument-sans: Commanding and heavy, Impact Label stands each letter apart like beads on a rod. Instrument Sans is the quieter partner, its plain sans strokes holding one weight from start to finish, while the heading does the shouting.
gen-dafont-impact-label-noto-serif: Impact Label hits hard, every letter standing alone with a high-set x-height and pincer-like c shapes. And Noto Serif, a text serif with a gentle thick-and-thin rhythm, would make the heading feel stranded if the heading were shrunk down.
gen-dafont-impact-label-roboto-slab: Heavy, blocky and unapologetic up top. Roboto Slab settles underneath with a slab-serif texture where the middle of the line dominates, giving the loud letters something structured to lean on.
gen-dafont-impact-label-rubik: Separate, bead-like letters give Impact Label a heavy, commanding stance. But Rubik, a soft sans-serif with a big lowercase and round shapes that stay legible small, handles the quiet work the heading never attempts.
gen-dafont-impact-label-space-grotesk: Impact Label towers with a high-set x-height and heavy, separate letters. Space Grotesk, a sans with a lower lowercase and hollow, breathing counters, would read lighter and easier paragraph after paragraph.
gen-dafont-impact-label-work-sans: Chunky, upright and loud, with every letter standing on its own like a bead on a rod. Work Sans, a sans-serif with stout strokes and wide-open c tips, sits beneath it quietly.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-fs-rowan: Jelly Crazies wobbles along with bowls that nearly seal shut. Rowan, a text serif with generous curves and thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones, opens things up beneath the goofy, tightly closed letters.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-noto-sans-ol: Wobbly, playful letters with bowls that almost close up define Jelly Crazies. Noto Sans Old Persian, a plain sans with open counters and a lofty lowercase, would let a longer passage breathe and move briskly.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-sono: Jelly Crazies brings playful wobble and bowls that nearly seal shut, with no calligraphic thinning anywhere in sight. Sono answers with a tall, widely spaced sans-serif whose a keeps its mouth ajar.
gen-dafont-joystix-fs-amulya: Amulya is a contemporary sans-serif whose curves keep generous gaps, so it reads easily. Over a longer passage it feels open and smooth, a clear break from the bold, widely tracked arcade lettering of Joystix.
